title: fix(update): recover from transient Windows package backup locks
body:
Refs #162027

## What Problem This Solves

Windows npm updates fail immediately when antivirus, indexing, or another process briefly holds the live package directory during its backup rename.

## User Impact

Updates can now finish after transient `EPERM`, `EBUSY`, or `EACCES` failures at that boundary. Each retry is recorded as a warning. Persistent failures still fail, name the source and backup paths, and preserve the installed package. The POSIX rename remains a single attempt.

This change belongs to the installed updater; a newer candidate cannot patch an already-running 2026.9.6 driver. The issue's separate exit-13 failure was already fixed in 2026.9.7 by #157042; this PR does not close the issue or claim to fix its repair-finalization symptoms.

## Why This Change Was Made

The swap owner delegates the backup rename to its existing filesystem owner. Windows uses the existing retry scheduler for 16 attempts with 250 ms initial backoff, capped at 5 seconds, totaling 57.75 seconds of waiting. Each attempt rechecks update authority, source/parent identity, and backup-path absence. There is no copy/delete fallback for the live package.

[Node's `fs.rename` reference](https://nodejs.org/docs/latest-v24.x/api/fs.html#fsrenameoldpath-newpath-callback) defines the rename/error contract. The explicit Windows antivirus-lock note is in [`graceful-fs`'s rename implementation](https://github.com/isaacs/node-graceful-fs/blob/v4.2.11/polyfills.js#L87), which documents locks lasting up to a minute and the same three retryable error codes; that note is not currently present in Node's `fs.rename` documentation.

The regression is registered in the existing `test:windows:ci:2` inventory. The actual changed-scope selector enables Windows for it, and the actual Windows planner assigns it exactly once to `checks-windows-node-test-3`.

## Evidence

Current head: `082f2afb988d22e36855dc9beb09ca735ec91002`. Production, regression, and documentation bytes are identical to the first transport commit `9e7674807a1acbfac85725074daca17be9244266`; the final commit only registers the regression in Windows CI.

Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01m3td6vgfack56gm1thz82jth` fetched the first commit directly, without a local tree sync, and installed with `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`.

- Before: the new boundary regression against the original production files failed 9 cases; all three transient-lock cases returned `failed`, and persistent lock cases attempted the rename only once. Two unchanged-behavior cases passed.
- After: all 11 cases passed, including two rename failures followed by success, persistent errors with preserved package/launcher bytes, POSIX/EXDEV non-retry, and authority/source/destination changes during backoff.
- Measured new-test cost: `pnpm test src/infra/package-update-swap.windows.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` took 18.19 seconds wall; compiler preparation took 13.568 seconds; individual tests took 9–52 ms (about 0.17 seconds total).
- Importing suites plus package-step siblings passed three times in the same file order: 28 files, 601 passed tests and 6 existing skips per run. Wall times were 761.14 seconds including initial shared E2E runtime preparation, then 185.30 and 184.61 seconds with that build reused.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base fa9e01430460eaac3eaf9bf25d34ff7c73435ff5` passed for the production/test/doc change, including core types, all 27 core-test type graphs, lint, formatting, dead-export scans, and selected guards.
- On fresh Testbox `tbx_01m3tfxx8hdryn5pvatnezssz1`, the complete final-head delta check passed: `CI=1 OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_REMOTE_CHILD=1 node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base 9e7674807a1acbfac85725074daca17be9244266`. It selected tooling only; no checks were substituted or skipped. The actual selector and Windows planner assertions also passed.
- Fresh direct-route P1 autoreview of the whole final branch against `fa9e01430460eaac3eaf9bf25d34ff7c73435ff5` passed: scoped-clean, no findings.

**Native Windows proof remains blocked.** The exact-head [Windows test job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36799311786/job/110170270287) on Node 24.21.0 selected the new regression and completed dependency installation, but the workflow was canceled during the tooling project before the infra project ran. There is no native Windows pass or per-file CI timing to claim. No workflow was rerun or manually dispatched for proof. ClawSweeper's requested native identity/upgrade validation and published-driver × candidate cell remain open before landing; the Linux fault-injection results do not replace them.

Production: +67/-4 lines (net +63); regression: +140 lines; docs: +8 lines; Windows inventory: one token added to an existing script. Production growth supplies bounded retries, per-attempt diagnostics, and identity/authority revalidation at the existing owner.

Auto-merge is intentionally off. This PR has not been merged.
